sentences: On RDNA every `s_barrier` counts against the same workgroup barrier and a wave that has ended no longer counts, while Vulkan requires a barrier to be reached by every invocation in uniform control flow.
Under `--wave64-emulate` the round loop keeps a single barrier at the top level, so this holds.

**Native wave32 compute shaders run in barrier rounds** when an `s_barrier` sits anywhere but a top-level block of the structured tree (one every invocation runs): under a guard, in a loop, or in the dispatch loop (`needs_barrier_rounds`, `bar_scheduler`).

That is the emulated loop without its cross-lane part: `s_barrier` ends a segment, each invocation runs its blocks until its next `s_barrier` or the end, then the whole workgroup meets at one `OpControlBarrier` (the same workgroup/acquire-release/workgroup-memory semantics) at the end of the round.
A wave that is done no longer holds the others, and a per-round count of the invocations not done (three `Workgroup` words, by round mod 3) ends the loop.
Cross-lane operations stay subgroup operations, as in the dispatch loop, since a wave's lanes run the same segment.
A barrier in a top-level block keeps the single `OpControlBarrier` in place.
In the 1.0.2.1 corpus 43 of the 55 wave32 cs shaders with `s_barrier` have one nested (SHADER-91's count), so those 43 now run in rounds.
Why: an Intel GPU does not survive the nested form.

`cs_barrier_divergent.asm` (two barrier sites in different branches), `cs_barrier_early_end.asm` (the other waves end without a barrier) and `cs_barrier_loop.asm` (a barrier in a loop whose trip count differs per wave) each lose the device (`vkQueueWaitIdle` → `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`) on an Intel Arrow Lake Xe-LPG iGPU (Windows 32.0.101.8132), and `cs_barrier_divergent` hangs or writes nothing on a UHD 770 (101.6129, #634).
With barrier rounds all three pass there and on an RTX 5070 Ti Laptop (617.42).
NVIDIA passed them before too (RTX 4070 Ti on 610.88 and 621.24, RTX 5090 on Linux 595.99, RTX 5070 Ti).

**Still not proven on the native wave64 path** (wave64 cs and every ms, run natively only on AMD's 64-wide subgroups): there the barrier stays where `s_barrier` is, inside a selection or loop construct in every ms and most wave64 cs shaders of the corpus.
Branches are scalar, so whole waves take the same path, and RDNA's own barrier counts the way the shader expects.
